The 2026 RSUE article is Xu, Guo, Zhong, and Shao, 'The impact of urbanization on child growth: Evidence from city-county mergers in China,' Regional Science and Urban Economics 117 (2026) 104187, DOI 10.1016/j.regsciurbeco.2025.104187. The paper-reported application concerns child stunting and wasting, with reported reductions of about 1.41% and 0.38% and mechanisms through nutrition supply, public services, and short-lived pollution mitigation. The existing record's E1–E6 evidence and 2011–2018 Bo–Wang replication define the currently grounded implementation regime, including separate prefecture/county exposure states and the need for legal crosswalks. The new article does not expose an inspectable complete merger list, county-level cohort/effective-date ledger, historical administrative-code crosswalk, exact child-health data source and joins, or the paper's treatment construction and sample exclusions. Its statement that implementation is centrally mandated/State-Council approved is a paper-reported institutional interpretation, not proof that all treated counties are exogenous. Do not extend or alter the canonical treatment timing from this abstract/preview evidence, and do not infer its 2000–2019 county coding from the Bo–Wang 2011–2018 replication. Retain this as a recent 2026 application lead; recency is only a light ordering signal. Reopen for an application update only with the target paper's inspectable full text/appendix, replication data, or an author manuscript that supplies the missing treatment and data links.

note: Blocked after a bounded evidence search on 2026-08-12. The RSUE article is a recent but soft-priority source: Mei, Su, Liu, Lan and Qiu, The economic impact of hydrogen energy infrastructure in China, Regional Science and Urban Economics 114 (September 2025), article 104143, DOI 10.1016/j.regsciurbeco.2025.104143. ESTABLISHED (full-text inspection of the published-version manuscript and Lincoln Institute WP19SF1, plus a located primary source):
- Identity: China's annual top-down farmland-to-urban-construction-land conversion quota regime. The central government's long-term plan, the Outline of National Comprehensive Planning on Land Use 2006-2020 (全国土地利用总体规划纲要), was approved by the State Council Standing Committee on 2008-08-13 and issued 2008-10-06 as State Council Document No. 33 of 2008 (国发〔2008〕33号); official text located at https://www.gov.cn/govweb/zxft/ft149/content_1144625_6.htm (the paper cites the same gov.cn interview series). The Outline sets the 1.8 billion mu cultivated-land red line and allows total developed land to rise from 31.92 to 33.74 million hectares over 2005-2010; province-level indicators are attached as tables (province-level quotas are public), and provinces then re-allocate their quota to prefectural cities.
- Key assignment fact: the exact central-to-province and province-to-city quota-allocation formula is not released, and sub-provincial quota and development information is not publicly available (paper's Section 2 states this explicitly). The 2016 adjustment (国土资发〔2016〕67号) revised the targets; implementation runs through annual land-use plans, with quota penalties for provinces failing the cultivated-land balance obligation (占补平衡).
- Paper application: the paper crawls the China Land Market website (www.landchina.com, maintained by the Ministry of Land and Resources), recording 1,941,657 transactions in March 2017 and analyzing 1,542,279 land-lease transactions for 2007-2016; city characteristics come from China City Statistical Yearbook 1995-2015 editions (covering 1994-2014). The paper documents actual city-level land conversion and land finance, estimates a city-level production function, and runs counterfactual reallocations of land quotas (e.g., 30% from inland to coastal, low- to high-productivity cities). It is descriptive/structural: no treatment-comparison construct, no timing exploit, no instrument.

NOT ESTABLISHED / BLOCKER: no observable rule that changes one unit's exposure relative to another is recoverable. City-level quota allocation is unobserved (the paper itself studies actual land supply, which equals quota plus adjustments plus violations, not the quota), the allocation formula is not public, and allocation is plausibly endogenous to city productivity, fiscal pressure, promotion incentives, and petitioning. A researcher cannot encode treatment from public data from this source; publishing a canonical record would be a policy-catalog entry without an assignment mechanism, which the serving gate rejects.

DEDUP: distinct from existing records china-anti-corruption-land-market (national campaign shock on land prices), china-land-property-rights-agricultural-efficiency and china-rural-land-titling-reform (rural tenure); distinct from the blocked industrial-land-minimum-price candidate (price-floor regulation vs conversion quota) and from queued candidates china-local-government-land-hoarding-land-price-system and China city export slowdown exposure and land-finance response (land finance/price and export-shock land-supply objects).

NEXT ROUTE: reopen only via a source that exploits an observable quota rule, e.g. a paper using 增减挂钩 (increase-decrease linkage) quota-transfer pilots, province-level annual land-use-plan quota series, or the 2016 Outline adjustment as an assignment; none such was in scope for this paper. Temp evidence files (.tmp_landconv*.pdf/.txt/.html) remain on disk for a later worker.

The treatment is a researcher-constructed measurement: DBI cluster status = county in top 5th percentile of 2-digit-industry firm counts from ASIFP 1998-2007 (firms >=5M RMB sales, ~90% of industrial sales, 2,815 counties; industry codes reconciled across GB/T 4754-1994->2002; boundary changes converted to a benchmark code system), plus OutputStrength/EstablishmentStrength (county share / national-mean share) and entrepreneurial shares OutputNonstate/EstablishmentNonstate (state capital <50% of paid-in capital). Exclusion restrictions are reported claims, not established facts: mining output (not reserves) is an economic activity endogenous to the commodity boom and policy with a documented resource-curse channel to county growth; church density correlates with missionary history and local development; classified highways plausibly affect rural income directly through market access and off-farm employment (the paper's own mechanism channel). It reports smaller flow declines in regions with greater diversification and vertical integration and additional moderation of nonlocal infection exposure, with heterogeneity by network centrality. This is a useful China-facing regional shock candidate, but lockdown intensity and infection exposure may be jointly selected with local conditions and the abstract does not establish a single exogenous rollout. Resolve must recover the truck OD units and dates, city/county crosswalks, exact lockdown or movement-control rules and timing, treatment/intensity/comparison coding, nonlocal infection and network-centrality construction, diversification and vertical-integration measures and pre-period, flow outcome and missingness, concurrent toll-free highway or reopening policies, spillovers and anticipation, wave-specific estimands, and overlap with any existing COVID or logistics variations. Keep it global-china-variation and do not call the lockdown universally exogenous.
note: Established (verified from OUP/EconPapers metadata and CUHK-SZ + PKU author news pages): paper identity Fang, Guo, Zhang (2023), JoEG 23(6):1345-1370, DOI 10.1093/jeg/lbad022; data are daily GPS records of ~1.8 million long-haul trucks in China, 2018-2020, used as proxy for intercity economic linkages; empirical object is the 2020 COVID outbreak and lockdown policy shock interacted with pre-existing regional diversification and vertical integration, with nonlocal infection exposure aggregated through the intercity trade network and heterogeneity by truck-network centrality. Missing (not recoverable from accessible sources): exact lockdown/movement-control rules and per-city timing, treatment/intensity/comparison coding, truck OD units and city crosswalks, diversification/vertical-integration construction and base period, nonlocal-infection aggregation formula, network-centrality measure, flow missingness, handling of the concurrent national toll-free highway policy (2020-02-17 to 2020-05-06) and reopening, anticipation/spillovers, wave-specific estimands. Full text is closed access: OUP page returns 403, Unpaywall is_oa=false with no OA location, Semantic Scholar openAccessPdf CLOSED, no preprint or replication package found; only citing-paper references located. Whether identification uses a uniform national shock with predetermined structure or selected local lockdown timing cannot be established from the abstract; do not call the lockdown universally exogenous.
